title: How Steve Jobs ran NeXT in 1992: software as the real advantage, patient management, and teams that agree
summary: At MIT Sloan in 1992, Jobs explains NeXT's strategy: attack operational productivity with object-oriented software, pair it with hardware so a direct sales force can create demand, and run the company through consensus among A-player executives. He also shares lessons from Apple, manufacturing, and technology windows.

principles.text: Your real competitive advantage often reveals itself only after launch; listen to customers and pivot fast.
principles.quote: a lot of times you don't know what your competitive advantage is when you launch a new product

principles.text: A product that is only 1.5-2x better won't win; you need a 4-5x advantage that makes it a must-have.
principles.quote: not one and a half or two times better than everything else but you know four or five times better than anything else where you had to have one

principles.text: Software advantages last far longer than hardware ones, so build around software for a defensible lead.
principles.quote: it's pretty impossible to get a sustainable competitive advantage from hardware

principles.text: Revolutionary products need a direct sales force to create demand; the existing channel only fulfills it.
principles.quote: the existing channel is only fulfilling demand

principles.text: The best code is the code you never write: fewer lines means faster to build, easier to maintain, nothing to break.
principles.quote: the code that's the fastest to write the code that's the easiest to maintain and the code that never breaks is the code you don't write

principles.text: Never compromise on hiring; keep chipping away for a year or more until you land the truly great person.
principles.quote: I've always found it best not to compromise and just keep chipping away
